Observation: For each index i, we want to consider elements j with j <= i - x (left side) or j >= i + x (right side). So for each i, we can check the minimum difference with any earlier element at distance >= x (i.e., among positions <= i - x) and any later element at distance >= x (i.e., among positions >= i + x). We can process using two passes: left pass with a data structure (balanced BST / sorted list) storing values of elements that are at least x behind (i.e., as we iterate i from 0..n-1, we insert nums[i - x] when i >= x into the sorted set, then query for closest value to nums[i] to get min diff for left side). Similarly, for right side we could similarly iterate from right to left, or we can treat similarly: while scanning left to right, we can maintain a sorted list of future elements? But easier: we can do left pass to compute min difference with any earlier element that is at least x behind; do right pass symmetric (or we could compute min with later elements by scanning reversed array). Since the condition |i-j| >= x is symmetric, scanning left to right and maintaining a sorted set of elements that are at least x behind i (i.e., inserted when we pass index i-x) ensures we consider all pairs where j < i and i - j >= x. Similarly we need pairs where j > i and j - i >= x. But scanning left to right and for each i, checking against earlier elements at distance >= x only covers pairs where the earlier index is at least x before i. However pairs where i < j and j - i >= x will be considered when we later reach index j and check earlier elements (i) that are at least x behind j. So indeed a single left-to-right pass checking earlier elements suffices for all pairs (i,j) with i < j, because when we reach the later index j, we will have inserted the earlier index i (if distance >= x) into the data structure. So we only need to check earlier elements that are at least x behind. That covers all unordered pairs.
